deep.reconstruction:
The page contains no mathematics. It is a draft of Riemann's philosophical essay on G. T. Fechner's Zend-Avesta and Nanna. It continues from 17r, where Riemann asks from what we infer that a body is ensouled, i.e. that a thought-process (Denkprozess) takes place in it. The argument is a chain of inductive and causal principles, not a derivation.

(P0) Footnote-type restatement from 17r: purposiveness that is conditioned, i.e. occurs within a bounded circle of appearances, must have a cause bounded in time and space. Unconditioned purposes are explained by an eternal Willing that is not produced by any temporal process.

(P1) The only purposive phenomena whose cause we perceive directly are our own actions. That purposiveness arises from willing the end and deliberating about the means.

A struck-out passage reframes the question as two sub-questions: does purposiveness occur that cannot be ascribed to the body itself, and is there ground to refer it to something larger?

(P2) Criterion. Suppose a body of ponderable matter contains a system of generative and causal relations (Zeugungs- und Wirkungsbezüge; the reading is uncertain) that is completely closed within it. Then we may explain it by a purposively acting process in that body. This explanation is the most probable when two conditions hold:
- (1) the purposiveness does not already close off within parts of the body;
- (2) there is no reason to seek its cause in a larger whole to which the body belongs.

This is in effect a maximal-closed-system criterion: locate the thought-process in the smallest body in which the purposive system is closed, provided no larger whole is indicated.

(P3) We actually judge the causes of purposiveness in humans, animals and plants by this criterion. Experience shows that in humans part of the purposive movements are caused by thought-processes in the soul (the word 'Gehirn' is struck out). Another part, the purposive organic processes, are not.

(P4) Application. Part of the purposiveness in humans, animals and plants is to be explained by a thought-process inside these bodies. The other part, the purposiveness of organisation, is to be explained by a thought-process in a larger whole. Three reasons are given:
- (1) Organic purposiveness does not close off within single organisms. The reasons for the arrangement of the human organism lie in the constitution of the whole surface of the Earth, organic nature included.
- (2) Organic movements repeat innumerably: side by side in different individuals, and successively in the life of one individual or one lineage. Hence a common cause, not a separate one in each case, must be assumed.
- (3) Organic arrangements undergo no further development within the life of an individual (humans and animals) or of a single lineage (plants and infusoria). Hence their cause is not a simultaneously running thought-process.

The next page applies the same principles to the Earth as a whole, yielding Fechner's Earth-soul as an inductive hypothesis.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics.
Philosophically, the step from 'repeated in many individuals' to 'common cause in a larger whole' is an inference to the best explanation, not a deduction.

Point 3 (no further development within an individual's or lineage's life) is an empirical claim in tension with transformist and evolutionary views. Riemann himself says on the next page that new, more perfect organisms appear over the Earth's history.

results.what: Criterion for locating the cause of purposiveness (a thought-process) in the smallest body within which a system of purposive/causal relations is closed, unless a larger whole is indicated; applied to separate individual purposiveness from organic purposiveness.
results.modern_name: Inference-to-best-explanation argument for panpsychism / world-soul (Fechnerian argument by analogy recast inductively)
results.usually_credited_to: G. T. Fechner (Nanna 1848, Zend-Avesta 1851); Riemann's critical restatement

deep.surprise_reason: This is part of Riemann's known philosophical fragments on Fechner and the Earth-soul. They were published in substance in the Nachlass section of his Gesammelte Werke (Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts), and his sympathy for Fechner is well documented. The page contains no mathematics and nothing novel.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely begins 'Für alle bedingte, d.h. in einem begrenzten Erscheinungskreise stattfindende Zweckmäßigkeit muß eine nach Zeit und Raum begrenzte Ursache gesucht werden', not 'die alle Bedingungen ... aus nach Zeit und Raum begrenzte Ursache'.
Line 3 probably reads 'in einem ewigen (in keinem zeitlichen Vorgange erzeugten) Wollen'.
'ein System von Zweck- und Wirkungs[?] Bewegungen' is more likely 'ein System von Zeugungs- und Wirkungsbezügen'. This matches the phrase on the next page.
'zweckmäßig wirkenden' is the insertion above the struck 'fortgesetzten'; the struck word near 'Vorgang' appears to be 'Denk-'.
The struck '[-Thie-]' before 'Thieren' is a false start. The phrase reads 'in Menschen, Thieren und Pflanzen'.
In point 3 the struck words after 'der einzelnen' are 'Geschlechter (Gattungen Arten)'. The sentence ends 'keine Fortbildung', with point 3 itself beginning 'erhalten'.
A short vertical note in the left margin is illegible and not transcribed.
